t: More than fifty countries were affected by the wave of revolutions between January 1848 and October 1849, but without significant coordination or cooperation among their revolutionaries.

Coalitions of workers and reformers, including members of the middle and upper classes, won early concessions in the spring of 1848, then divided; conservative forces and armies suppressed most of the revolutions, killing tens of thousands of people.
Many of the revolutionaries' goals were achieved within about two decades, largely by their opponents: serfdom ended in Austria and Hungary, and Hungary gained more self-determination in 1867.
dyk: When news of the revolution in France reached Vienna, the Austrian chancellor Klemens von Metternich is said to have exclaimed, in French, "well, my dear, it's all over!"; a few weeks later he resigned and went into exile.
ev: A revolution in Palermo, Sicily, begins the wave of revolutions in January
King Louis Philippe I abdicates on 24 February and the French Second Republic is proclaimed
Fighting in Vienna in March forces Metternich to resign, and barricade fighting in Berlin leads Frederick William IV to withdraw the army
The June Days uprising of Paris workers is suppressed by General Cavaignac, and Louis Napoléon Bonaparte is elected French president in December
King Frederick William IV of Prussia rejects the imperial crown offered by the Frankfurt National Assembly
The Roman Republic falls to French intervention in July and Venice surrenders in August
Hungary surrenders to Austria and Russia on 13 August, and the fortress of Komárom falls in October

f.where: Europe, above all France, the Italian states, the Austrian Empire (including Hungary and the Czech lands) and the states of the German Confederation; smaller risings in Denmark, Switzerland, the Romanian Principalities and Ireland; echoes in Latin America and the Dutch East Indies
f.period: revolution in Sicily January 1848; February Revolution in France and the March risings in Germany, Austria, Hungary and Italy; counter-revolution from May to December 1848; a second wave in 1849 ending with Hungary's surrender in August and the fall of Komárom in October 1849
f.figures: Louis Philippe I, the French king who abdicated; Klemens von Metternich, Austrian chancellor, who resigned; Lajos Kossuth, leader of the Hungarian government; Giuseppe Mazzini, organiser of Young Italy; Frederick William IV of Prussia, who refused the imperial crown; Louis Napoléon Bonaparte, elected French president in December 1848
f.outcome: most revolutions were suppressed, tens of thousands were killed and more went into exile; lasting reforms included the end of serfdom in Austria and Hungary, the end of absolute monarchy in Denmark and representative democracy in the Netherlands
